newsitem.title: MEXICO: RESEARCH ALERT - Mexico's Bital started.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Mexico's Bital started.

text.p: --Santander Investment initiated coverage of Mexican Grupo Financiero Bital with a buy rating.

--Santander sees earnings per share to rising to $0.13 for 1996, $0.08 for 1997 and $0.15 for 1998 versus a loss per share of $0.24 in 1995, and predicts a 12- to 18-month target price of $1.14 that would be up 50 percent from the current level.

-- Analysts Laura Z. Berdeja and Robert Lacoursiere praise CEO Antonio del Valle Ruiz for focusing on raising capital, improving the funding mix, expanding the branch network, revamping systems and cleaning up loan portfolio of Banco Internacional, Bital's largest subsidiary.

-- Banco Internacional, also known as Bital, is seen as market innovator with a growing market share because of growing number of branches, all of which are open Saturdays, and becoming the first bank to eliminate account fees.
-- "While we believe that the stock merits a discount for liquidity, operationaal risk and future dilution, it does present a very attractive investment," Berdeja and Lacoursiere write.
-- Low funding costs and high client base make Bital well-positioned for greater-than-average earnings growth, the analysts say.
